thread:
Rae T: Quick sync re: postmortem follow-ups. Action items keep aging out. proposal: mandatory owner + SLA per action type and automated reminders. thoughts?

Diego M: big +1. 'team' ownership is the problem. what SLAs do you have in mind?

Rae T: starting point: monitoring/config -> 7d, infra/code -> 21d, security -> triage in 72h then 14-21d depending on severity. owners assigned at publish.

Nina S: can we also add a recurrence flag so items from repeat incidents get escalated? two incidents in 30d -> high recurrence.

oncall-bot: I can create follow-up tickets when a postmortem is published. sample fields: owner, type, due, recurrenceScore (0-5), links. I will ping owner at 48h and 3 days before due; escalate 48h after overdue.

Diego M: good. closure criteria? owners should have a checklist: deploy/verify, runbook updated, short lessons learned, metrics to watch.

Rae T: yes, add closure checklist to ticket and require a 1-3 bullet lessons-learned. also require runbook links.

Nina S: rotation: IC = current oncall, backup = previous oncall. require a 48h handover note for active incidents when IC changes.

Diego M: operational ask: track follow-ups in Jira with a stable label and dashboard filter. spreadsheet is fine short-term but not for audits.

Rae T: plan: I'll draft the SLA matrix + closure checklist and create a Jira issue type. pilot for next 4 incidents. who wants to help wire the bot?

Nina S: I'll help with the recurrence scoring logic and pilot reviews.

Diego M: I'll do the Jira workflow and dashboard.

oncall-bot: Created pinned template for follow-ups (link: https://redwood.fake/pin/followup-template).

Rae T: thanks — I'll post the draft SLA + timeline by Wednesday and schedule a 15-min pilot review.

Diego M: ack.

Nina S: ack.

Rae T: closing loop: action owners assigned in-thread and bot will create tickets on publish. we'll revisit after pilot.
